newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says telecoms pact will add jobs, markets.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says telecoms pact will add jobs, markets.

text.p: President Bill Clinton, hailing a landmark deal to open global telecommunications markets, said on Saturday the United States would reap significant economic benefits.

"Today's agreement will bring clear benefits to American workers, businesses and consumers alike -- new jobs, new markets and lower prices -- and will spread the benefits of a technology revolution to citizens around the world," the president said in a statement issued by the White House.
"This important agreement advances our interests and opens new opportunities for growth, prosperity and progress," he said.

Earlier, negotiators in Geneva representing some 70 countries reached a breakthrough agreement opening up nearly all of the world's telecommunications markets after months of talks under the auspices of the World Trade Organisation. The deal was struck just hours ahead of a deadline.

Clinton said the agreement would open markets for the basic telecommunications services that use information technology goods -- computers, telephone equipment and semiconductors -- for which the United States led efforts two months ago to eliminate tariffs around the world.
"These are critical steps toward realisation of the American vision of a global information infrastructure," he said.
